title: Atomic‐Scale Insights Into the Thermal Stability of High‐Entropy Nanoalloys

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Possibly a multi-element alloy mixture (e.g., CoCrFeMnNi) in nano-particulate form
recollection.intervention: Guess: They employed in situ high-temperature analyses (e.g., TEM or XRD) to evaluate alloy stability
recollection.structure: Guess: A single-phase high-entropy nanoalloy with uniform elemental distribution
recollection.mechanism: Guess: High configurational entropy suppresses phase separation and stabilizes the alloy at elevated temperatures
recollection.results: Guess: The nanoalloys remained alloyed with minimal segregation up to several hundred degrees Celsius

score.note: The recollection only generically suggests in situ high-temperature characterization. It misidentifies the alloy, omits the FCC multi-twinned/icosahedral structure and Au/Cu surface segregation, and proposes entropy-driven stabilization—the opposite of the reported surface-energy-driven diffusion and kinetic instability. No correct quantitative values are recalled.
